newsitem.title: UK: Euro vegoil traders trim prices but remain cautiou.
newsitem.headline: Euro vegoil traders trim prices but remain cautiou.

text.p: European vegetable oil traders trimmed prices during Tuesday afternoon but remained cautious after the latest USDA data.
News that the USDA had left its soybean carry-over figure at 140 million bushels in its latest report led traders to expect a much sharper drop on the Chicago market that in fact happened.
"Chicago should be limit-down on these figures, but the funds have some very long positions to protect and won't give up without a fight," said one trader.
Traders said there was also some doubt over the data released by the USDA.

"People still feel the carry-over should have been nearer to 110 to 120 billion bushels because if we are to believe what we are told exports have been running at a much higher rate than the USDA said," one said.
Traders said they expected the export figures to be up from February's 905 million bushels, instead of down to 900 million.
"We were looking for a figure nearer to 915 to 920 million and it would surprise no-one if next month's figures were a lot higher," said another trader.
However, others said despite the doubts there was still a very good crop in Brazil and that alone should be enough to bring the market down.
No new business was reported after the USDA report with most players waiting to see where Chicago settles and how the Malaysian markets react on Wednesday.
Dutch soy oil closed two to 0.25 guilders up and tradeless while rape oil was 0.50 guilders higher to unchanged after Apr traded at 105.50 and Aug/Oct at 106.50 and 106.75 guilders a 100 kilos.
Crude palm oil closed $2.50 to $5 up while products were unchanged to $2.50 higher.

Coconut oil closed with sellers mixed at $2.50 up to $7.50 down after Mar/Apr traded at $745 and May/Jun at $735 in outright business while Apr/May traded at $740 in a switch with Jun/Jul at $730 a tonne.
Palmkernel oil finished unchanged and tradeless.
